Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:10:1.english: Where a scribe is not commonly available - The scribe is not constantly present in the town.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:10:2.english: A scribe happened to come his way - And he went ahead and wrote [the marriage contract] prior to betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:11:1.english: In one [act] - He said: “Behold, both of you are betrothed to me.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:11:2.hebrew: אינן מקודשות - ואין אחת מהן צריכה גט, ובגמרא מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:11:2.english: Neither of them is betrothed - And neither one of them requires a bill of divorce, and in the Gemara [it] explains the reason:

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:11:3.english: And it was of the Sabbatical Year - The Gemara explains what this comes to teach us.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:12:1.hebrew: בשעה שנעשו צרות זו לזו - כגון שקדשן כאחת. קס"ד דקרא בהכי כתיב, וקאמר ״לא תקח״ — אין לך בהן לקוחין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:12:1.english: At the time that they become rival wives to one another - Such as when he betrothed them simultaneously. It entered [Rami bar Ḥama's] mind that the verse was written regarding this [case], and it says, “You shall not take” — you have no [valid] betrothal with them.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:12:2.hebrew: אי הכי - דקרא בבת אחת כתיב, היכי מיחייב כרת אם בא עליהן? הרי אין כאן איסור אחות אשה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:12:2.english: If so - That the verse is written regarding [betrothing them] simultaneously: How is he liable for excision [karet] if he engages in intercourse with them? Behold, there is no prohibition of a wife’s sister here.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:13:1.hebrew: אלא בזה אחר זה - שבקידושין הראשונה היא אשתו, וקאמר: אין קידושין תופסין באחותה, ואם בא עליה — ענוש כרת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:13:1.english: Rather, consecutively - For through betrothal, the first [woman] is his wife, and [the verse] states that betrothal does not take effect with her sister, and if he engaged in intercourse with her, he is punished with karet.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:13:2.hebrew: ומתניתין - כי היו נמי בבת אחת, מהאי קרא נפקי, וכדרבה. וסברא בעלמא הוא: כל שאינו בזה אחר זה, אפילו בבת אחת אינו. הלכך, כיון דבאחות אשה לא תפסי קידושין, כי קדשינהו בב"א נמי לא הוו קידושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:13:2.english: And the mishna - That even when they were [betrothed] simultaneously, [the ruling] is derived from this verse, and in accordance with [the principle of] Rabba. And it is merely logical reasoning: Whatever cannot [take effect] sequentially cannot [take effect] even simultaneously. Therefore, since betrothal does not take effect with a wife's sister, when he betrothed them simultaneously, it also does not constitute betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:1:1.hebrew: אינה מקודשת - ולא אמרינן: יודע היה שאין קידושיו קידושין, וגמר ושלח סבלונות לשם קידושין; אלא אמרינן: מחמת קידושין הראשונים שלח:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:1:1.english: She is not betrothed - And we do not say: He knew that his betrothal was not a [valid] betrothal, and [so] he resolved and sent gifts for the sake of betrothal; rather, we say: He sent [them] on account of the first betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:1:2.english: And similarly, a minor who betrothed - And sent bridal gifts after he reached majority.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:2:1.hebrew: וצריכא - למיתני שתי נשים בפרוטה, ולמיתני או אחת בפחות משוה פרוטה, וקטן שקידש — לאשמועינן בכולהו דסבלונות דבתר הכי לאו לקידושין ניתנו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:2:1.english: And it is necessary - To teach [the case of] two women with [one] peruta, and to teach "or one [woman] with less than the value of a peruta," and a minor who betrothed — to teach us in all of them that the gifts [sent] afterward were not given for betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:2:2.hebrew: טעי - וסבר דקידושין נינהו, ולא מסיק אדעתיה דסבלונות לשם קידושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:2:2.english: He errs - And thinks that they are [valid] betrothals, and it does not enter his mind that the gifts [are] for the sake of betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:4:1.hebrew: חוששין לסבלונות - מי ששידך באשה ונתרצה, וקדם ושלח סבלונות בעדים — חוששין שמא קידושין הן. ואם נתקדשה לאחר, צריכה גט מן הראשון:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:4:1.english: One is concerned about gifts - One who arranged a match with a woman and she consented, and he went ahead and sent gifts in the presence of witnesses — one is concerned that perhaps they are [an act of] betrothal. And if she became betrothed to another, she requires a bill of divorce from the first.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:4:2.english: And Rabba similarly says - [This] is the reading.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:4:3.english: And we raise an objection against our teaching - I have an objection to raise against my words:

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:4:4.hebrew: התם כדקתני טעמא דטעי כו' - בקידושי קמאי וסמיך עלייהו, אבל האי דלא קידש — איכא למיחש להכי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:4:4.english: There, as the reason is taught: That he was mistaken, etc. - [He was mistaken] regarding the first betrothal and relied upon it; but this one, who did not betroth [her beforehand], there is reason to be concerned about this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:5:1.hebrew: התם כדקתני טעמא דטעי כו' - בקידושי קמאי, וסמיך עלייהו. אבל האי דלא קידש — איכא למיחש להכי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:5:1.english: There, as the reason is taught, that he erred, etc. - [He erred] regarding the first betrothal, and he relied upon it; but this one, who did not [first] betroth, there is reason to be concerned about this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:6:1.english: Where he did not enter into the category of betrothal at all - And he did not bring [the thought of] betrothal to mind.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:6:2.hebrew: אבל הכא דנחית להכי - ומתוך שעלה על לבו ונזכר שאין קידושיו כלום, ושלח סבלונות — אימא לשם קידושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:6:2.english: But here, where he entered into this - And since it occurred to him and he remembered that his betrothal was nothing, and he sent bridal gifts, [one might] say [that they were sent] for the sake of betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:7:1.hebrew: חיישינן - דכיון דאורחייהו לקדושי ברישא, חיישינן דשדר הני לשם קידושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:7:1.english: We are concerned - For since it is their custom to betroth first, we are concerned that he sent these [gifts] for the sake of betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:9:1.english: A marriage contract was established in the marketplace - That they saw a marriage contract.

Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:9:2.hebrew: מהו - אם נתקדשה לאחר, מהו להחזיקה כמקודשת לראשון:
Rashi on Kiddushin 50b:9:2.english: What is [the halakha] - If she became betrothed to another, what is [the ruling regarding] presuming her to be betrothed to the first?

Tosafot on Kiddushin 50b:12:1.hebrew: לא תקח - פי': לא יהא לך ליקוחין בה. תימה: אם "לא תקח" משמע שאין ליקוחים תופסים בה, א"כ אמאי תפסי קידושין בחייבי לאוין, כגון אלמנה לכ"ג, וגרושה וחלוצה לכהן הדיוט? הא כתיב בהן "לא תקח"! וי"ל, דלא ממשמעות ד"לא תקח" דרשי', אלא משמע ליה דה"פ דקרא: "ואשה אל אחותה לא תקח" בבת אחת — פירוש: לכל אחת ואחת יש דין אחות אשה ואסורה; ואחות אשה נפקא לן בפרק האומר (קדושין דף סז:) דאין קידושין תופסין בה, דחייבי כריתות היא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 50b:12:1.english: "You shall not take" - Meaning: You shall not have [valid] "taking" (betrothal) with her. [This is] difficult: If "you shall not take" implies that betrothal does not take effect with her, if so, why does betrothal take effect with those [forbidden by] negative commandments, such as a widow to a High Priest, and a divorcee or a chalutzah to an ordinary priest? Behold, regarding them it is written: "You shall not take"! And one can say that we do not expound [this] from the [literal] meaning of "you shall not take"; rather, he understood that this is the explanation of the verse: "And a woman to her sister you shall not take" simultaneously — meaning, each one has the legal status of a wife's sister and is forbidden; and [as for] a wife's sister, we derive in the chapter [entitled] "HaOmer" (Kiddushin 67b) that betrothal does not take effect with her, as she is among those liable to excision [karet].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 50b:12:2.hebrew: אי הכי היינו דכתיב ונכרתו הנפשות העושות ואי קידושין לא תפסי כרת מי מחייב - וקשה, דאמרינן ביבמות פרק ארבעה אחין (יבמות דף כח:) גבי שלשה אחים, שנים מהם נשואים לב' אחיות, דרבי שמעון פוטר בשתיהן מן החליצה ומן הייבום, שנאמר: "אשה אל אחותה לא תקח לצרור" — בשעה שנעשו צרות זו לזו. אלמא משמע: אע"ג דקידושין לא תפסי, יש בהם כרת, כיון שפוטר אותם מן החליצה ומן הייבום! וי"ל: דשאני התם, דליכא למיפרך כדפריך הכא: "כרת מי מחייב?", דבלא הקידושין נמי איכא כרת — דקא פגע באשת אחיו שלא במקום מצוה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 50b:12:2.english: "If so, is this that which is written: 'And the souls that do [them] shall be cut off'? And if betrothal does not take effect, is one liable for karet?" - And [this] is difficult, as we say in Yevamot, in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achin (Yevamot 28b), regarding three brothers, two of whom were married to two sisters, that Rabbi Shimon exempts both of them from chalitzah and from yibbum, as it is stated: "And you shall not take a woman to her sister, to be a rival" — at the time that they become rival wives to one another. Evidently this implies: even though betrothal does not take effect, there is [liability for] karet regarding them, since he exempts them from chalitzah and from yibbum! And one can say: It is different there, for one cannot challenge [it] as [Rava] challenges here, "Is one liable for karet?", since even without the betrothal there is also [liability for] karet — for he encounters [the prohibition of] his brother's wife not in the context of a mitzvah.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 50b:4:1.hebrew: חוששין לסבלונות - פי' בקונטרס: ששידך האשה ונתרצית, וקדם קודם הקידושין ושלח סבלונות בעדים — חוששין שמא לשם קידושין שלח. משמע מתוך פירושו דחיישינן שמא מחמת קידושין הם, ולכך נקט בלשונו "שידך", דאל"כ לא הוו קידושין, דמנא ידעה, כדאמר בפ"ק (לעיל קידושין דף ו.) גבי נתן לה קידושין ולא פירש. וקשה להר"ם: וכי שידך, מאי הוי? והא בעינן שידבר מענין לענין ובאותו ענין! לכך נראה לפרש "חוששין", כלומר: כיון ששלח לה סבלונות, חיישינן שמא קידשה כבר. וכן משמע בסמוך, דקאמר: "באתרא דמקדשי והדר כתבי כתובה חיישינן", והתם על כרחך צריך לומר דחיישינן שמא קידש כבר, דלשון "חיישינן שמא לשם קידושין שלח" לא שייך, דהא פשיטא דלא שילח לה הכתובה לשם קידושין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 50b:4:1.english: One is concerned about gifts - [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres: Where [a man] proposed to the woman and she agreed, and prior to the betrothal he went ahead and sent gifts in the presence of witnesses, we are concerned that perhaps he sent [them] for the sake of betrothal. It is implied from his explanation that we are concerned that perhaps they are [given] on account of betrothal. And for this reason he formulated in his phrasing [that he] "proposed," for if not so, they would not be [valid] betrothal, as from where would she know? As [the Gemara] states in the first chapter (above, Kiddushin 6a) regarding one who gave her betrothal [money] and did not specify. And it is difficult to the Ram: Even if he proposed, what of it? Behold, do we not require that he speak from matter to matter and [be dealing] with that same matter? Therefore, it appears [correct] to explain "one is concerned" — that is to say: Since he sent her gifts, we are concerned that perhaps he already betrothed her [previously]. And so it is implied nearby, where [the Gemara] says: "In a place where they betroth and then write a marriage contract, we are concerned." And there, perforce one must say that we are concerned that perhaps he already betrothed [her], for the phrasing "we are concerned that perhaps he sent [it] for the sake of betrothal" is not applicable, as it is obvious that he did not send her the marriage contract for the sake of betrothal.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 50b:8:1.hebrew: ה"ג מקדשי והדר מסבלי פשיטא - דמקודשת. כלומר: היכא דשלח סבלונות קודם הקידושין — דמקודשת, דדלמא לשם קידושין שלח. וי"מ: פשיטא דמקודשת — דאמרי' דקידשה כבר, והוי כמו שפירשתי. ומשני: לא צריכא, דרובא מקדשי והדר מסבלי, ומיעוטא מסבלי והדר מקדשי; מהו דתימא ניחוש למיעוטא — פי' ולא תהא מקודשת? קמ"ל דאזלינן בתר רובא ותהא מקודשת. וקשה: דהיכי קאמר ניחוש למיעוטא והוי להקל?! מיהו אין זו קושיא, דה"נ אשכחן בכמה דוכתין (גיטין דף יט:): חיישינן שמא במי מילין כתבו, והוי חששא להקל, והוי גיטא מכל וכל; וכן בריש פ' אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין דף לב.): שטר שכתוב בו זמנו בשבת או בעשרה בתשרי כשר — חיישי' שמא אחרוהו וכתבוהו. ור"ח גרס איפכא: לא צריכא, דרובא מסבלי והדר מקדשי, ומיעוט מקדשי והדר מסבלי; מהו דתימא לא ניחוש למיעוטא — פירוש שלא תהא מקודשת? קמ"ל דחיישי' למיעוטא ותהא מקודשת; והשתא ניחא, דחיישינן למיעוטא משום חומר דאיסור אשת איש. והשתא הא דקאמר רב פפא "באתרא דמקדשי והדר מסבלי" — היינו שמיעוטם מקדשי והדר מסבלי, ואפ"ה חיישי' למיעוטא; "מסבלי והדר מקדשי" — היינו שכולם מסבלי והדר מקדשי. אך ר"י מצא כתוב גירסא אחרת: "מסבלי והדר מקדשי פשיטא" — דלא חיישינן ואינה מקודשת; לא צריכא, דרובא מסבלי והדר מקדשי, ומיעוט מקדשי והדר מסבלי; מהו דתימא ניחוש למיעוטא ותהא מקודשת? קמ"ל:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 50b:8:1.english: This is the text reading: "Where they betroth and afterward send gifts, it is obvious" - [It is obvious] that she is betrothed; that is to say, where he sent gifts before betrothal, that she is betrothed, for perhaps he sent [them] for the sake of betrothal. And some explain: It is obvious that she is betrothed, because we say that he already betrothed her, and this is in accordance with what I explained. And [the Gemara] answers: "No, it is necessary [in a place where] the majority betroth and afterward send gifts, and a minority send gifts and afterward betroth. Lest you say: Let us be concerned for the minority" — meaning: and she would not be betrothed — "[Rav Pappa] teaches us" that we follow the majority, and she is betrothed. And it is difficult: For how can it say "let us be concerned for the minority," when that would be to be lenient?! However, this is not a difficulty, for we also find so in several places: (Gittin 19b) "We suspect that perhaps he wrote it with gallnut water," and this is a suspicion [applied] to be lenient, and it is a completely valid bill of divorce; and similarly at the beginning of the chapter [entitled] Echad Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 32a): A document in which its date is written on Shabbat or on the tenth of Tishrei is valid, [as] we suspect that perhaps they postdated it and wrote it. And Rabbeinu Chananel reads the reverse: "No, it is necessary [where] the majority send gifts and afterward betroth, and a minority betroth and afterward send gifts. Lest you say: Let us not be concerned for the minority" — meaning, that she should not be betrothed — "[Rav Pappa] teaches us that we are concerned for the minority, and she is betrothed"; and now this works out well, for we are concerned for the minority due to the stringency of the prohibition of a married woman. And now, that which Rav Pappa said: "In a place where they betroth and afterward send gifts" — that is where a minority of them betroth and afterward send gifts, and even so we are concerned for the minority; "where they send gifts and afterward betroth" — that is where all of them send gifts and afterward betroth. However, the Ri found a different reading written: "[Where] they send gifts and afterward betroth, it is obvious" — that we are not concerned and she is not betrothed; "No, it is necessary [where] the majority send gifts and afterward betroth, and a minority betroth and afterward send gifts. Lest you say: Let us be concerned for the minority and she shall be betrothed — [Rav Pappa] teaches us [that we are not concerned for the minority]."
